extracted.intended_audience: national and local governments, parliamentarians, civil society organizations, and others interested in Open Government Partnership membership
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and categories for participation in the Open Government Partnership (OGP), covering national/state membership, affiliate participation, local government membership (OGP Local), and parliamentary engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: State membership eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State that is a member of the United Nations or any Specialized Agency of the United Nations, without prejudice to its international recognition status, may become an OGP member by adhering to the terms for participation outlined in the Articles of Governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Becoming a national member requires adherence to the OGP Articles of Governance (terms for participation). The statement implies that UN membership or membership in a UN Specialized Agency is the baseline eligibility criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate participation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdictions that do not fall under these two categories, but that are members of a major intergovernmental organization or forum, may participate in OGP as affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliates are for jurisdictions not qualifying as UN/UN Specialized Agency member states but that belong to a major intergovernmental organization or forum. The page groups these under 'Affiliates and Non-Voting Members' and links to further information ('Learn more').

rubrics_metrics.name: Local government participation (OGP Local)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local governments — whether a state, prefecture or municipality — may join OGP Local, a stream launched in 2016 to build partnerships between local governments and civil society organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGP Local focuses on local governments because they are closest to citizens and can deliver innovative open government reforms. Participation is intended to foster open, inclusive, participatory, and accountable governance at the local level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliament engagement pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliaments can engage with OGP; the page directs readers to a separate 'Parliaments in OGP' resource for information on how parliaments can engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page does not enumerate criteria here but points practitioners/legislators to the dedicated resource for guidance on parliamentary participation and engagement with OGP.
